newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia cancels Busang gold contract bids.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia cancels Busang gold contract bids.

text.p: Indonesia's mines minister said on Wednesday the government had cancelled parliamentary approval for an application for contracts of work by Canada's Bre-X Minerals Ltd for the huge Busang gold find.
"We cancel it. The Bre-X contract of work will be processed from the beginning," minister Ida Bagus Sudjana told reporters following a marathon parliamentary commission hearing.
The cancellation was the latest twist in a drama over one of the world's richest finds, estimated by Bre-X to contain at least 57 million ounces of gold, in East Kalimantan province.

The secretary-general of the Mines and Energy Ministry, Umar Said, told the hearing the government was checking with the Indonesian Capital Markets Supervisory Agency (Bapepam) regarding representations Bre-X had allegedly made as to its status on Busang to the New York Stock Exchange Commission.

The Indonesian government has been pushing Alberta-based Bre-X and the big Canadian mining company Barrick Gold Corp to form a 25-75 partnership to develop Busang. The government also wants a 10-percent stake in the find.
Bre-X has said it had yet to complete a deal with Barrick as it would need shareholders' approval.
Bre-X has a contract of work for the Busang I area of the property on Borneo island.
But Busang I contains only an estimated 2.6 million ounces of gold, with the bulk of the precious metal in two adjoining lots, Busang II and III for which it still needs COWs to explore and develop.
Parliamentary approval is the first step in the process of granting contracts of work (COWs).

Bre-X had received the parliamentary go-ahead for its Busang II and III COWs in July and approval from the Investment Ministry in September. But they were then held up as a result of a dispute over ownership of the property.
Sudjana earlier told the commission hearing that processing of the application for contracts of work by Bre-X was suspended because it did not meet administrative conditions.
Umar reiterated that Bre-X and Barrick had informed him on December 4 that they had completed a deal to develop Busang.
"Bre-X and Barrick have also agreed not to include any new players in the project," he said.
"Bre-X has asked for time to get its shareholders' approval over its partnership with Barrick, and the government has taken note of the request," he added.
